newsitem.title: USA: NYS resident challenges "lulus" for Assembly.
newsitem.headline: NYS resident challenges "lulus" for Assembly.

text.p: New York State resident Robert Schulz, who has sued the state over various financial and other issues, on Monday said he was challenging a decision to grant stipends to a handful of members of the Assembly.

Schulz, who heads the All-County Taxpayers Association, a 2,000-member advovacy group for what it calls "good government," said the state failed to meet a constitutional deadline for approving the stipends, called "lulus," by year-end.

The legislature was unable to agree on the controversial measure during a one-day special session held in December, but it was approved on January 21, after the start of a new legislative term. The suit was filed in the State Supreme Court for Albany County.

Further, Schulz said that the state Appellate Court affirmed a ruling by the New York State Supreme Court that requires H. Carl McCall, the state comptroller, to appear at a hearing to fix the amount of damages assessed against him, in his individual capacity.
A spokesman for the comptroller was not immediately available to comment.
Schulz had charged that the comptroller sought to influence a 1995 vote on a measure called Proposition 3, which covered debt-reform.
